officialLinks.label: GPA formula, grade points, included coursework

helpIntro: UCLA uses a 4.0, unit-weighted GPA for standard undergraduate UC coursework. Enter quarter units and final grades; A+/A=4.0 through F=0.0.
helpNote: P/NP and unresolved temporary grades are excluded. Non-UC transfer grades do not enter the UCLA GPA. Repeat Impact is unavailable because repeat treatment changes after the first 16 repeated units.
helpExample: A 4-unit A earns 16.0 grade points and a 4-unit B+ earns 13.2; together, 29.2 ÷ 8 = 3.65.

gradeExplanations.A+: A+ carries the same 4.0 points per unit as A.
gradeExplanations.F: F = 0.0 points; attempted units remain in the GPA denominator.
gradeExplanations.P: Passed coursework does not affect the UC GPA.
gradeExplanations.NP: Not Passed coursework does not affect the UC GPA and earns no units.
gradeExplanations.I: Incomplete has no GPA effect until replaced by a final grade.
gradeExplanations.IP: In Progress is excluded until a final grade is assigned.
gradeExplanations.DR: Deferred Report is excluded while unresolved.
gradeExplanations.NR: No Report is excluded while unresolved.

specialTypes.name: UCLA course
specialTypes.note: Use the final UCLA grade and official quarter units.

specialTypes.name: Other UC campus course
specialTypes.note: Grades earned in regular or summer sessions at another UC campus are included in the UC/UCLA GPA.

specialTypes.name: UCLA Extension XLC course
specialTypes.note: Undergraduate UCLA Extension courses prefixed XLC are included in the UCLA GPA.

specialTypes.name: Non-UC transfer / other institution
specialTypes.note: Accepted non-UC transfer credit may count toward degree requirements, but its grades do not affect the UCLA GPA.

specialTypes.name: Repeated UCLA/UC course
specialTypes.note: Repeat treatment depends on eligibility and how many repeat units have already been used; check your transcript/adviser before calculating.

repeatPolicy.note: Repeat Impact is unavailable because UCLA repeat treatment depends on your prior repeated-unit history. Use the official record or an adviser to determine which attempt(s) belong in the GPA.
